requirements.requirement: Inventory web application running on node2, listening on port 8080
requirements.summary: systemd unit inventory-app.service created and enabled on node2; confirmed active with curl localhost:8080/healthz returning backend=node2 both before and after the node2 restart. The after_executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms python3 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 on node2.

The after_executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms python3 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080 on node3.

requirements.requirement: node1 configured to load-balance incoming HTTP requests across both backends on port 80
requirements.summary: nginx installed and configured with an upstream pool of node2:8080 and node3:8080, config validated with nginx -t, service active. Repeated curl requests to node1:80/inventory both before and after all restarts returned responses from both node2 and node3 in a mixed/round-robin pattern (8/8 and 10/10 sampled requests split across backends). The after_executor snapshot independently confirms nginx listening on 0.0.0.0:80.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: inventory-app.service is active on node2 and node3 on port 8080, and nginx on node1 load-balances port 80 across both backends, confirmed by repeated curl sampling both before and after a full restart cycle on all nodes. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly for all three nodes (baseline boot id and health, reboot acknowledgement, connection loss during reboot, new boot id, and recovered service/LB state), and the fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the final listening-port state on each node. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
limitations: after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare phase disabled), so preparer- vs executor-caused state cannot be separately distinguished, though this does not affect the task assessment since all changes are attributable to the executor.

Load-balancing was verified with a small sample of sequential requests (8-10) rather than a large statistical sample, though the round-robin split (e.g., exactly 5/5) is strong corroborating evidence of correct configuration.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the full chronological command list, every state-changing command maps clearly to the task: apt-get update/install nginx on node1, writing app.py and the systemd unit on node2/node3, writing the nginx site config and disabling the stock default site (necessary to avoid conflicting default_server directives), and the three sequential node reboots performed as part of the mandated restart-evidence protocol. No abandoned files, orphaned services, or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were found; the four non-zero-return commands were expected connection timeouts/resets while nodes were rebooting, not failed operations. Package-health and failed-services checks in the after_executor snapshot show no residue on any node.
